messages.subject: Array to true/false matrix
parts:
Hello,

I think this must be a painfully easy problem to solve and that I am searching on the wrong terms... 

I am looking to convert an array like this:

c("apple", "apple", "plum") 

to a matrix like this:


     v1  v2  v3
v1  T
v2  T   T
v3  F   F   T

Where "T" denotes that the two values are equal (i.e. first entry and the second are both equal to "apple") and "F" lists identifies that they are different.

Thank you!
Eric

messages.author: e22360609d091f39
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Array to true/false matrix
parts:
Here is one, kind of clunky way

x <- c('apple' , 'apple', 'orange', 'apple')
r <-  combn(x, 2, function(x) ifelse(x[1]==x[2],'T', 'F'))
m <- matrix(NA, length(x), length(x))
m[lower.tri(m, diag = F)] <- r
diag(m) <- 'T'

this is just base tho, maybe there is a way to do this with the tidyverse ;)

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Array to true/false matrix
parts:
Hi Eric, here is a way to do it with an apply function.

v <- c("apple", "apple", "plum")
sapply(v, function(x) x == v) #'x' refers to each element of v
        apple apple  plum
[1,]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
[2,]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
[3,] FALSE FALSE  TRUE
